title: GCLI-89 review follow-ups: pin the base-rebinding-by-attribute-name category and the ruled fixture pair
description: Non-blocking findings from the Opus delta on opum-ai/glyph-cli#139 (verdict APPROVE at c86215c, merged as 4f313f7). Not started. (1) Medium: base also rebound attribute names and identifier subscript indices, so head now resolves bare-name calls the base reported as rebound, for example def helper(): ...; obj.helper = 1; helper(). Add a fixture and sample one or two real sites. (2) Low: put the ruled literal pair (clean() beside with_attr_assign()) in one test. (3) Low: fixtures for a subscript target in a for or comprehension target, and an attribute target in a comprehension. Informational: the fix can resolve a wrong edge where the analyzer has no rule for monkeypatching (self.m = f; self.m(); self.__class__ = Other; k.m = f; k.m(); module monkeypatches); that is the static-binding design as ruled.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a fixture pins that obj.helper = 1 does not make a bare-name call helper() rebound, red on 1d2441d and green on dev
the ruled pair clean() and with_attr_assign() is asserted in one test
fixtures cover a subscript target in a for target, a subscript target in a comprehension target, and an attribute target in a comprehension target
one or two real sites of category (1) are sampled and their correctness recorded
